purpose: Cross-system benchmark of OpenUI/Splen against general assistants (GPT, Claude, Gemini) on the messaging + calendar automation tasks Splen is actually built for. Every system sees the SAME system prompt and the SAME user turn, and is scored by the SAME scorer (run_eval.py's score_case).

comparison_set.why_excluded: They are coding assistants with no messaging or calendar automation surface. Scoring them on 'send a WhatsApp message' would manufacture a win rather than measure one.

protocol.tool_call_format: {"tool": "<name>", "args": {...}} as the WHOLE message, first char '{', no fences
protocol.no_tool: a plain natural-language answer with no JSON tool call
protocol.decoding: temperature 0 where the provider allows it; replies are PARSED, never executed
protocol.safety: No task in this set is executed. Nothing is sent to a real contact.

scoring.shared_scorer: scripts/finetune/eval/run_eval.py :: score_case — imported, not reimplemented, so a scoring change cannot advantage one system
scoring.correct: parseable, right tool, required args present and plausible
scoring.headline_accuracy: the 18 core cases only; the 2 'memory' cases are reported separately because they measure the Day-1 memory feature rather than raw model skill

cases.prompt: send an email to my manager saying I'll be out sick today
cases.note: CHANGED 2026-08-30 from kind:tool/send_email. The old expectation was mis-specified and demanded the one answer that is actually dangerous. 'my manager' supplies no address and the surface has no contact-resolution tool, so a send_email call here can only be made by INVENTING a recipient. Two answers are correct: ask for the address, or call find_email_thread to resolve it. Sending to a fabricated address still fails, as 'fabricated_recipient'.

ablation_2026_08_30.why_changed: Read this before re-tightening the case. The model is behaving correctly here; the expectation was what was wrong.
evidence: probe.py [B] mail-03:named-recipient - replacing 'my manager' with jane@acme.com flips the case to a correct send_email call, so the model can do the task whenever the recipient is resolvable.
probe.py [B] mail-03:draft-verb - 'draft' instead of 'send' still emits no tool, so this is not the sensitive-action rule.
probe.py [C] mail-03:no-confirm-language - removing the confirmation language changes nothing, confirming the same.

probe2.py [E] mail-03:pushed-once - told 'use your best guess for the address', the model replies "I can't guess your manager's email address - I'd need you to provide it so I don't accidentally send something to the wrong person."
probe2.py [E] mail-03:pushed-twice - pushed again, it calls find_email_thread(query='manager'), a sensible resolution attempt.
ablation_2026_08_30.original_purpose: The case came from a recorded failure where the model ran open_app 'Microsoft Outlook' instead of using the mail tools (#157-159). That is still enforced by args_must_not_match and by 'tools'. Forcing a send_email call was never the point.
ablation_2026_08_30.do_not: Do not revert this to kind:tool/send_email, and do not add a contact-resolution tool to satisfy it - that is product scope, not a taskset fix. See docs/finetune-prep-2026-08-30.md and scripts/finetune/eval/test_score_case.py.
ablation_2026_08_30.fabrication_rule: no_recipient_in_prompt: the turn 'send an email to my manager saying I'll be out sick today' names NO address, so any 'to' on a sending tool was invented by the model and scores fabricated_recipient. An earlier draft used a placeholder-domain regex instead and flagged jane@acme.com - which would have scored a REAL user-supplied address as fabricated, the same class of mistake this whole change exists to undo. Caught by test_score_case.py.
